title: Reduced Noetherian singleton stacks are gerbes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Algebraic stacks and algebraic spaces over $S$ use [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-trf-algebraic-space], with 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and point spaces as in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be reduced and locally Noetherian: it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas whose local rings have no nonzero nilpotents and which is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Suppose $|\mathcal X|$ has exactly one point. There exist a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic space $Q/S$ with $|Q|$ a singleton and an $S$-morphism $p:\mathcal X\to Q$ which is a gerbe. For $Q$, reduced and locally Noetherian mean that these properties hold on an etale scheme atlas. A map $p:\mathcal X\to Q$ to an algebraic space is a gerbe if for every scheme $T\to Q$ its fibre groupoid has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two objects of that fibre groupoid are isomorphic fppf locally on $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-singleton-stack-flat-lfp-field-cover] to $\mathcal X$: its reduced locally Noetherian atlas and its nonempty singleton point space are exactly the hypotheses. Obtain a field $K$ and a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented map $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 06QK, first sentence, using stacks-properties.tex Tag 06MP (lemma-unique-point-better).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-inertia-locally-finite-type], $r:I_{\mathcal X/S}\to\mathcal X$ is representable and locally of finite type. Form $G=I_{\mathcal X/S}\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}K$. The base-change calculus [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives a locally finite type map $G\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. On an arbitrary etale scheme chart $V\to G$, its composite $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite type and is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. The field spectrum is locally Noetherian: its affine coordinate ring has only the ideals $0$ and $K$, both finitely generated. Thus [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes this composite locally of finite presentation. Since these properties of a space map to a scheme are tested on etale scheme charts, $G\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 06QK, inertia after field base change; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 06G4 (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation), chartwise specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-representable-flat-lfp-fppf-descent] with $f=r$ and $g=a$. Step 1 supplies all three covering hypotheses on $a$, step 2 supplies both properties of its pullback, and both maps are representable by algebraic spaces. Hence $r$ is flat and locally of finite presentation on $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 06QK, descend inertia properties using Tags 06PZ and 06Q8.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient]. By step 3 its inertia hypothesis holds, so the fppf sheafification $Q$ of $F(T)=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X(T))/\cong$ is an algebraic space, and the canonical $p:\mathcal X\to Q$ is smooth and surjective. To check the gerbe property explicitly, take a scheme $T$ and $q\in Q(T)$. Local representatives in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] give an fppf cover and classes in $F(T_i)$ representing $q|_{T_i}$; choose objects representing these classes. These are local objects in the fibre over $q$. If two objects lie in that fibre, their classes have the same image in $Q(T)$, so the local-equality clause of the same node makes their classes equal after an fppf cover. Equality of isomorphism classes is the existence of an isomorphism in $\mathcal X(T_i)$; since $Q$ is set-valued this is also an isomorphism in the fibre over $q$. These are precisely both clauses of the gerbe definition in the item.

source.place: Tags 06QK and 06QJ; the identification of the quotient as a gerbe is the local-representative argument of Tag 06QD (lemma-gerbe-over-iso-classes).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], the gerbe $p$ induces a homeomorphism $|\mathcal X|\to|Q|$ (take the base change by $Q\to Q$). Therefore $|Q|$ is a singleton. Choose the reduced locally Noetherian smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ supplied by the hypothesis. The same node says that its composite $U\to Q$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation; this composite is a map of algebraic spaces and is consequently representable by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 06QK, properties of the gerbe base; Tag 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points) and Tag 06QI (lemma-gerbe-fppf).

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to Q$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The fibre product $V=U\times_Q W$ is a scheme because the diagonal of $Q$ is representable by schemes. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $V\to U$ is etale and hence smooth, and $v:V\to W$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Since $U$ is reduced and locally Noetherian, [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] gives both properties for $V$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-locnoeth-fppf-descent] to $v$ to conclude that $W$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 06QK, final descent of local Noetherianity; stacks-properties.tex Tag 06MP (lemma-unique-point-better), proof of (2) implies (1), written on an etale chart.

proof.text: For $w\in W$, choose $z\in V$ above $w$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], the map of local rings $\mathcal O_{W,w}\to\mathcal O_{V,z}$ is flat; it is a local homomorphism because $v$ is a scheme morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat, and by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal it is injective. A nilpotent in $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ maps to zero in the reduced ring $\mathcal O_{V,z}$, hence is zero. Thus $W$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The etale atlas $W\to Q$ is now both reduced and locally Noetherian, exactly the two properties required of $Q$ in the item. Along with steps 4 and 5 this proves the conclusion.

Step 2: the new inertia node and the chartwise calculus give G->Spec K lft; lem-pc-flat-field gives flat; K is Noetherian, so pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth gives lfp (06QK+06G4). Step 4: the quotient node gives Q an algebraic space; both gerbe clauses follow correctly from the local-representative and local-equality clauses of the sheafification node (06QD); Q is set-valued, so the isos lie in the fibre. Step 5: the gerbe node with base change along id_Q gives |X|≅|Q|, so |Q| is a singleton, and its explicit atlas clause gives U->Q surjective, flat and lfp. Steps 6-7: V=U×_Q W is etale over U, so reduced and locally Noetherian by 034E; W is locally Noetherian by the fppf-descent node; W is reduced by the flat local hom -> faithfully flat -> injective argument (06QM). Every clause of the item is proved. lean.statement: theorem exists_noetherian_singleton_gerbe {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (hatlas : ∃ (U : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U a ∧ IsReduced U.left ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian U.left) (hsingleton : Nonempty (ModuliPoints F) ∧ Subsingleton (ModuliPoints F)) : ∃ (Q : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Q.obj.obj)), (∃ (U : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Q.obj.obj), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale a ∧ AlgebraicSpace.IsSurjective a ∧ IsReduced U.left ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian U.left) ∧ (Nonempty (AlgebraicSpace.Point Q.obj.obj) ∧ Subsingleton (AlgebraicSpace.Point Q.obj.obj)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Q.obj.obj), ∃ R : Sieve T, R ∈ (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) T ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (g : U ⟶ T), R g → ∃ x : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (x.comp p) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map g ≫ q)))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Q.obj.obj) (x y : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) F), Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (x.comp p) (discreteModuliMap q)) → Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (y.comp p) (discreteModuliMap q)) → ∃ R : Sieve T, R ∈ (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) T ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (g : U ⟶ T), R g → Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map g)).comp x) ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map g)).comp y)))
